title: Crop and scale an image
summary: Trim a photo with the Crop tool, then change its size with Scale Image.

steps.say: Open a photo with Control O, or check that one is already showing in the middle.

checks.prompt: Is an image open and visible in the middle of the GIMP window?

hints: Use File, then Open, and pick any JPG from your Pictures folder.
Dragging a photo file onto the GIMP window opens it too.
steps.why: Every edit needs an open image to act on.

steps.say: Press Shift C to pick the Crop tool.

checks.prompt: Is the Crop tool selected in the toolbox, with crop settings in Tool Options?

hints: Tools, then Transform Tools, then Crop in the menu bar also picks it.
Click on the image first so GIMP has focus, then press the keys.
steps.why: The Crop tool trims the outer parts of an image.

steps.say: Drag across the photo to draw a rectangle around the part you want to keep.

check.prompt: Is a crop rectangle drawn on the photo, with the area outside it darkened?

hints: Drag the edges or corners of the rectangle to adjust it.
Tick Fixed in Tool Options to lock a shape such as a square.
steps.why: Framing first shows exactly what stays before anything is removed.

steps.say: Press Enter to apply the crop.

checks.prompt: Has the photo been trimmed and the crop rectangle gone?

hints: Clicking inside the rectangle applies it too.
Control Z undoes the crop if you change your mind.
steps.why: The crop is only a preview until you confirm it.

steps.say: Open the Image menu at the top and choose Scale Image.

checks.prompt: Is the Scale Image dialog open with Width and Height boxes?

hints: The Image menu sits in the menu bar between View and Layer.
Press Alt and I to open the Image menu from the keyboard.
steps.why: Scale Image changes how many pixels the whole image has.

steps.say: Type 1200 in the Width box, press Tab, then click Scale.

checks.prompt: Is the Scale Image dialog closed and the image smaller than before?

hints: Keep the chain icon beside Width and Height joined so the photo does not stretch.
Check that the unit menu next to the sizes shows px, which means pixels.
steps.why: A smaller pixel size makes the file lighter for email and the web.
